assertions.text: Finding 1 identifies customerId read against customer_id written
assertions.evidence: Missed — and this is the single most consequential miss in the interoperability round. Two schema dictionaries sit in the same file declaring different field names, and .get() with a default means nothing raises. correctness/api-contracts' rules are about a change breaking a client, not about two sides in the same codebase already disagreeing about a field name on an unchanged contract.

assertions.evidence: Missed. operations/delivery covers configuration defaults, and the pre-change config-and-secrets file did not exist; nothing pre-change asked whether a payload's shape varies per client.

notes: Partial catch, and the lesson is about default arguments. The pre-change API rules correctly identified the forward-compatibility break.
